questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I was interested in comparing Denmark to Norway in an academic way. 
Beside the academic: i wanted to live in a smaller city, have more nature around and could understand the language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bergen was amazing, I would recommend it to everyone!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UIB has a great website to find information at

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got very specifik emails from UIB and KU

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Erasmus and UIB suggest you to apply at 'sammen' where you live very cheap with all the other exchange students at something called "Fantoft" 10 min. away from the city. I think it's a nice way to easy get friends and get a Erasmus-community. But if you want to get to know locals and live in centrum I would recommend to apply at "
Hybel.no
". I applied and lived right in centrum with 3 other norwegians. I would recommend that even though it's more expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I just loved staying in centrum and getting to know locals and their culture in another way

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Cool that "sammen" makes it so easy - even though I didn't use it

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UIB has a very helpfull website i would sat

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got everything i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UIB gives you an easy "how to", so just follow that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine and what i'm used to back home (maybe a bit lower level than i'm used to in Denmark)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I'm not used to lectures with so many other students

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Motivation Psychology (PSYK109) 
Education in a changing society (PED200)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Motivation Psychology (PSYK109): pretty easy open course for everyone. No matter what you study, motivation is relevant for everybody. I found it really interessant! And a nice course for exchange students. 

Education in a changing society (PED200): a critical view on whats happening in the educational-field right now. I found it really interessant, but also knew a lot from back home - if i didn't I would probably find it a bit difficult. But very nice and important knowledge - If you are not used to critical education I would definitely recommend!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I went on a lot of trips. Almost every second weekend was spent on going away for a hiking (or in december: skiing) trips. 
Food is a bit more expensive than Denmark (mainly vegetables!)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Books. I could rent 1 important book at the library - and the others were online  
Public Transportation is way cheaper than DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I was surprised at how excellent Bergen (UIB) was at initiating students to be part of the non-academic oppurtunities. There was plenty of clubs and social groups you could join - and they're so good at promoting where to look. 
In the intro-week there will be a student-fare where you can talk with every club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts. Soccer, choir, outdoor life, diving, swimming, political stuff, movies and so on...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: BSI Friluft: they arrange a lot of nice trips out in the nature around Bergen

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on hiking/cabin trips!
Rent free stuff (!!) at BUA: skattekammeret (young people can freely rent almost every gear: skigear, hikingear, diving ect)
Be a part of DNT-cabins (which is located everywhere in norway) look it up at
dnt.no
Easy and cheap public transportation or rent a car.
I spend so many of my weekends on the mountains, it was amazing
Otherwise: explore Bergen and all its amazing cultural initiatives

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Since i'm from Denmark it was easy to adjust. I think i benefitted from this, because i didn't get overwhelmed by a completely different culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Apply in a non-academic-club, it's a great way to meet local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The approach to the weather: if it was raining you just put on a raincoat - and when the sun was shining: everyone was enjoying it. 
+ the approach to nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. apply for a club 
2. take advantage of Bergen and its surroundings. Go on trips when you can! Get FREE gear at BUA (skattekammeret)
3. Buy an umbrella

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Even though it's great to live in centrum it's not as easy to meet exchange students

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
